matches.quote: The fitted gaps (≈1.2 meV at Tc = 2.1 K) imply 2Δ/kBTc ≈ 13, well above STM values (≈0.25 meV), which suggests non-ideal contact effects.
The PCS data therefore carry no information on B2u versus B3u, and the assignment rests entirely on the external NMR result of ref. [31].
With realistic broadening, and with an anisotropic Au gap ... the split peak could easily merge into a single ZBCP. ... Fit the S1–S3 data with Au
the quantitative conclusions lean heavily on a fit whose parameters are poorly constrained ... Au cannot be excluded ... and that ZBCPs can have extrinsic origins.
The authors rule out heating only at ambient pressure, where there are no dips ... Show the magnetic-field dependence of the dip positions at 0.6–1.2 GPa
Show best fits at 0.6 and 0.8 GPa with Δz/Δx(y) constrained to the ambient value of 0.57 while Z and Γ are free.
the fit has at least seven parameters for one spectrum, so the double-dip 'fit rather well' is not a stringent test.
A generic continuous transition out of a B2u state produces a mixed B2u + (i)B3u multicomponent state, not a pure B3u state
If the double dip reflects a genuinely multicomponent order parameter, such as B2u + B3u, a superposition of two single-IR channels is not the physically right model.
Pressure data come from only one contact, so junction evolution cannot be separated from bulk order-parameter evolution.
No contact resistance, Sharvin/Maxwell estimate or contact diameter is given to establish the ballistic regime.
Table S1 gap columns are swapped relative to Fig. S7, Fig. S9 and the main-text conclusion
No parameter-correlation analysis, χ² landscape or fixed-ratio comparison fit is given to show that the dips 'can only' be reproduced by a larger pz weight.
It is not stated whether Z and Γ, which look nearly constant, were fixed across temperature.

notes: C10 is judged 'raised' because P9 explicitly identifies the single pressurized contact as preventing separation of junction evolution from bulk order-parameter evolution, even though it asks for constrained fits rather than new measurements. C17 and C19 are 'partly' matched by P3 (questioning physical validity of linear channel superposition for multicomponent states rather than interband coupling) and P13 (noting constant Gamma across T and asking if it was fixed). C27 is 'partly' matched by P2, P6, and P9, which argue the ZBCP and side-dips are model-dependent and do not rule out fully-gapped Au.
